back: The stable plant community in equilibrium with the regional climate. Rainforest is the climax of the humid tropics.
A subclimax is held back by a natural factor such as fire or grazing animals; a plagioclimax is held back or altered by human activity such as burning or clearing.
Emergent trees, canopy (about 25–40 m), understorey and shrub layer, and a dark forest floor.
Drip-tip leaves shed water, buttress roots support tall trees, lianas and epiphytes reach the light, and the leaves are evergreen.
Deciduous leaves, deep tap roots, thick fire-resistant bark, thorns and small leaves, and grasses that grow from the base.
A deep, red or yellow, leached and acid soil of the humid tropics, rich in iron and aluminium oxides and kaolinite, with a thin humus layer and low fertility.
Intense chemical weathering in a hot, wet climate in which silica and bases are leached out and iron and aluminium oxides remain.
Savanna soils: shallower than oxisols, with clearer horizons, more humus from grass roots, moderate fertility and a risk of erosion.
Turnover time = litter store ÷ annual litter input (for example 0.9 t/ha ÷ 10 t/ha a year = 0.09 years).
